title: Video to Frames
dek: MP4 or WebM in — a folder of PNG or JPG stills out. Every frame, or one every N seconds.
meta: Extract PNG or JPG frames from MP4/WebM video in your browser — all frames or every N seconds. Free, no uploads, your video stays local.

steps.p: MP4 and WebM are the well-trodden paths. Short clips finish fastest.
One frame per second is the sane default; 'every frame' for stop-motion work. Format: PNG for crispness, JPG for volume.
Frames arrive in a ZIP, named in order.

faq.q: The first use takes a while — why?
faq.a: A 31 MB video engine has to load into the page first. It happens once per visit, on your machine, and it's the only big download the whole site has.

faq.q: How long can the video be?
faq.a: Guided by memory: a few minutes of 1080p is fine. For an hour of footage, a desktop video editor will be kinder to you.

title: Video to GIF
dek: Properly palette-tuned GIFs — the kind that don't look like a weather radar from 1998.
meta: Turn a video clip into a clean, palette-optimised GIF in your browser. Set the frame rate, size and range. Free, no uploads.

steps.p: Trim to the good bit first — GIFs are heavy, so seconds, not minutes.
12–15 fps loops read as smooth. 320–480px wide is the useful size range.
The palette pass is done twice so the colours come out clean instead of muddy.

faq.q: Why do GIFs get so big?
faq.a: It's a 1987 format with no real compression — every frame is a full picture. That's why the size settings matter here more than anywhere else on this site.

faq.q: GIF or MP4 — which should I share?
faq.a: Every platform since 2010 takes MP4, at a tenth of the size. GIF survives where videos autoplay silently (chat apps, forums), which is its one advantage.

title: Video to Audio
dek: Pull the soundtrack out of a video — MP3 for everything, WAV when it needs to be raw.
meta: Extract MP3, WAV or OGG audio from any video in your browser. Choose the quality, keep it lossless. Free, offline, no uploads.

steps.p: Anything the engine can read — MP4, WebM, MOV, and friends.
192 kbps MP3 is transparent for most ears. 320 for music. WAV for editing or archiving.
The video file itself is untouched; you just gain the soundtrack.

faq.q: Can I extract from a protected or rented video?
faq.a: No, and the tool won't pretend otherwise — copy protection exists precisely to stop this step, and the engine will simply fail to read it.
Voice: 128 is plenty. Music: 192–320. Archiving or editing: WAV, no question.

title: Compress Video
dek: Big video, smaller file, still watchable. Dial in the quality and see the savings before you commit.
meta: Compress MP4 and WebM video with quality control and optional resizing. Runs locally in your browser — no uploads, no waiting queues.

steps.p: The current size is your baseline.
High keeps things visually identical. Medium is the sweet spot — often half the size. Low is for 'send it over any connection'.
720p is plenty for messaging and most viewing. Then compress and compare the numbers.

faq.a: Video compression is genuinely heavy work, and this runs on your CPU rather than a rack of servers. A one-minute clip at Medium takes a couple of minutes.
Yes, with a modest audio bitrate so it doesn't undo the savings.

title: Trim Video
dek: Keep the goal, cut the walk-back. Set the start and end seconds and take exactly that slice.
meta: Trim MP4 and WebM video clips by start and end time, browser-based and fully offline. No re-encoding headaches, no uploads.

steps.p: The duration is read out so you can plan the cut.
In seconds, or in minutes-and-seconds format, e.g. 1:30. The preview player helps you find the moment.
You get exactly the slice, fast, because the untouched parts aren't re-encoded.

faq.a: Where possible, no — the file is cut at keyframes and copied as-is, which is fast and lossless. Precision trimming of a couple of seconds may trigger a light re-encode.

faq.q: Can I save multiple clips in one go?
faq.a: One clip per pass for now; run the tool again on the same video for the next highlight.

title: Convert Video
dek: MP4, WebM and MOV — the three the web actually speaks. Swap between them without a desktop app.
meta: Convert video between MP4, WebM and MOV in your browser. Choose codec and quality. Free, private, no uploads or accounts.

steps.p: Almost any common format is readable.
MP4 (H.264) is the universal choice. WebM is web-native and smaller for screen recordings. MOV for Apple editing chains.
Quality presets keep it simple: High, Balanced, Small.

faq.q: Why can't I convert to AVI or WMV?
faq.a: Those formats are comfortably past their usefulness for the web, and the engine here is kept lean on purpose. MP4 has been the sane answer since 2008.

faq.q: What's the best format for a website?
faq.a: MP4/H.264 for compatibility everywhere, WebM as a smaller second source if you want to serve the best to modern browsers.

title: Mute Video
dek: Delete the soundtrack without touching a single frame — smallest possible operation, cleanest possible result.
meta: Strip the audio track from MP4 or WebM video and keep the picture bit-for-bit. Browser-based, instant where possible, no uploads.

steps.p: The audio stream is detected and shown.
The video data isn't re-encoded — the picture stays exactly as it was.
A silent version, usually produced within seconds.

faq.a: No. This removes an entire stream; the picture stream is copied untouched, byte for byte.

faq.q: Can I replace the audio instead?
faq.a: Not here — muting is the safe, common operation. Mixing new audio in deserves a proper editor.

title: Audio Converter
dek: MP3, WAV, OGG, M4A, FLAC — the everyday roster, converted both ways, at the quality you choose.
meta: Convert audio between MP3, WAV, OGG, M4A and FLAC in your browser. Bitrate control, batch friendly, no uploads. Free.

steps.p: Batch is fine — an album of WAVs to MP3 takes a few minutes, unattended.
MP3 at 192 for general use; WAV or FLAC when something downstream needs lossless.
Files come out one by one, or all together in a ZIP.

faq.a: No — a 128 kbps MP3 re-saved at 320 is still 128 kbps of real information in a bigger coat. Lossless outputs from lossless inputs are the only honest upgrade.
Both work. M4A is AAC in an Apple-shaped box — common from phones and voice memos.

title: Trim Audio
dek: Cut a ringtone out of a song, a clip out of a lecture, a mistake out of a recording.
meta: Trim MP3, WAV, OGG and M4A audio by start and end time, right in your browser. No upload, no re-download from a server. Free.

steps.p: The duration and format are shown immediately.
Start and end in seconds or m:ss. Play your original alongside to find the spot.
You get the clip in the same format as the original.

faq.q: Can I fade in or out?
faq.a: Not built in — trimming is a clean cut by design. A DAW or Audacity will do fades better than a checkbox here ever would.

faq.q: Does trimming an MP3 re-compress it?
faq.a: Only the cut edges are re-encoded, the frames between are copied. In practice: inaudible.
